01 · Executive summary

One controlled material journey, from receipt to production

TrackGRN is a responsive plant material traceability application. Every physical pack receives a unique label identity and every operational change is persisted through the API into Microsoft SQL Server with user, time and status history.

02 · Solution architecture

Clear separation between operator UI, business API and data

The monorepo contains two independently deployable applications. The UI never writes directly to the database; all validation, authorization, lifecycle transitions and audit creation pass through the ASP.NET Core API.

Operator devicesDesktop · Tablet · Zebra handheld
→
TrackGRN UIReact 19 · TanStack · PWA
→
TrackGRN APIASP.NET Core 8 · JWT · validation
→
Microsoft SQL ServerEF migrations · transactions · audit

Printer adapter: Simulation for demo · Windows spooler / Zebra TCP for plant deployment

Security boundary

JWT authentication, role-based API authorization, strong password hashing and short-lived access tokens.

Database lifecycle

Versioned EF Core migrations, idempotent seed data and separate commands for migrate, seed and normal API startup.

Hardware strategy

Keyboard-wedge scanning works without a vendor SDK. Printing can switch from simulation to configured plant hardware.

03 · End-to-end business flow

GRN-to-production lifecycle

The guarded lifecycle prevents an unreceived or duplicate pack from being consumed and keeps the exact GRN, material, label, operator and station relationship traceable.

→
2Validatepreview & warnings
→
3Create GRNrevision controlled
→
4Generate labelsunique pack UID
→
5Print / reprintreason audited
→
6Inward scanreceive pack
→
7Issue scanstation required
→
8Trace & reportcomplete history

Accepted transition

Generated → Printed → Inwarded → Issued
Each successful action records quantity, user, timestamp and operational context.

Blocked transition

Duplicate inward, duplicate issue, issue-before-inward, inactive station and restricted GRN revision are rejected with clear feedback.

Hardware boundary for client demo

Scanner entry can be demonstrated with a keyboard or attached keyboard-wedge scanner. Printing remains in simulation until the target Zebra/Windows printer is physically available; production adapters are already represented in the backend.

07 · Demonstration readiness

Recommended client demonstration sequence

Live scenario

  1. Sign in and review dashboard KPIs.
  2. Import a valid SAP GRN Excel workbook.
  3. Open the GRN and review material packs.
  4. Generate/preview labels in simulation mode.
  5. Inward one label, then issue it to a station.
  6. Trace the UID and show the SQL-backed audit timeline.

Deployment modes

Client/UAT: cloud UI + cloud API + Azure SQL free allowance.

Plant production: LAN/on-prem API and SQL Server for internet-independent operation and local printer reachability.

Current demo: local UI/API with SQL Server Express and simulated label printing.

Conclusion: TrackGRN is ready for a controlled client demonstration and UAT walkthrough. Final production acceptance should include the real SAP workbook format, physical Zebra scanner/printer and plant network environment.
